title: Sell Mineral Rights in Louann, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Louann, AR
metaDescription: Louann, AR mineral rights in Ouachita County, a small oil town with production dating to the region's mid-century Smackover development. Get a written offer.
heroLead: Louann is small even by Ouachita County standards, but its name shows up on enough old lease documents to make clear the town had its own working oil field once.
intro: The Louann oil field was one of several smaller Ouachita County discoveries that produced steadily through the mid-twentieth century without ever drawing the attention that El Dorado or Smackover did. Mineral ownership in and around town tends to be quiet and inherited, small interests held by families who leased their land once, generations ago, and have received modest royalty checks or none at all since.

sections.heading: A Small Field With a Real Production History
paragraphs: Owners near Louann sometimes assume their mineral rights are inactive simply because they've never received a check, but a lease can go dormant without the underlying mineral rights losing their value, particularly given renewed regional interest in the Smackover Formation's brine potential. Confirming current status starts with a title search, not with the absence of a royalty statement.

sections.heading: Getting Ownership Sorted Out
paragraphs: As in most of Ouachita County, tracts near Louann were frequently passed down through inheritance without formal probate, leaving several family members as undivided co-owners without a clean paper trail. The Ouachita County Circuit Clerk's office in Camden holds the records needed to establish who owns what, and an affidavit of heirship is usually sufficient to resolve gaps left by an unprobated estate.

faqs.question: I've never received a royalty check from land near Louann. Do I still own mineral rights?
faqs.answer: Likely yes, unless you specifically sold or conveyed them. A lack of production or an inactive lease doesn't erase mineral ownership; it just means nothing is currently generating income from it.

faqs.question: Is the old Louann field still producing anything?
faqs.answer: Some legacy wells in the area continue at low, declining volumes typical of a field this age. Others have been plugged. Current status is specific to each well and unit.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my interest is inside a newer brine unit?
faqs.answer: We can check your legal description against current Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission unit filings to see whether your tract falls within an active or proposed brine unit.

faqs.question: How long does it typically take to sell a small Louann-area interest?
faqs.answer: Once title is confirmed and paperwork is complete, straightforward sales of a clearly owned interest usually move quickly, often within a few weeks.
